description:
Why this issue exists: outbound.rs percent_encode_msgid() only encodes '<', '>', '@', and space. Message-IDs can legally contain '/', '?', '#', '%', and other URL-significant characters (RFC 5322 §3.6.4 allows a wide range of printable ASCII in the local-part). A message-id like '<../../../etc@host>' would produce a URL path traversal. A '#' in a message-id would silently truncate the URL at the fragment boundary. '%' in a message-id would produce double-encoding corruption.

What needs to be done: Use a proper percent-encoder (e.g. the percent-encoding crate with PATH_SEGMENT encode-set, or url::form_urlencoded). At minimum, extend the match to cover '/', '?', '#', '%', '+', '=', '&', and all non-ASCII bytes.
title: percent_encode_msgid: incomplete encoding allows path traversal in AP URLs
